brief.meaningEn: Turn pages casually to get an initial impression without reading every line.
brief.meaningZh: 隨手翻頁，先大概看看內容，而非逐字細讀。
brief.grammar: Leaf through + a book, magazine or it; leafed is the past form. The object follows through.
brief.register: Library browsing: a reader tells a friend how she chooses a magazine article.
brief.boundaryZh: 隨手翻閱不等於已細讀或查證全文，也不表示讀者一定喜歡。
brief.misconceptionZh: 這裏 leaf 是翻頁動詞，不是樹葉；也不是用搜尋功能精確查字。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分辨初步瀏覽與細讀，說出翻閱後還要作甚麼判斷。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 139, row 7; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: I like to leaf through it before choosing an article.

listening.en: Mira leafed through the magazine before choosing an article; she looked at headings but had not read any story fully.
listening.zh: 米拉選文章前先隨手翻閱雜誌；她看了標題，還未細讀任何故事。

options.en: Turned pages casually for an overview.
options.zh: 隨手翻頁以了解大概。

options.en: Read every article closely.
options.zh: 仔細讀完每篇文章。

options.en: Picked leaves from a tree.
options.zh: 從樹上摘葉。

options.en: Searched for one exact word with software.
options.zh: 用軟件搜尋某個確切詞語。

listening.explanationZh: 她只看標題，屬初步翻閱。

reply.promptEn: Why did Tomas pause before borrowing a recipe book? He turned several pages, glanced at pictures and headings, and then decided which chapter to read at home.
reply.promptZh: （托馬斯借食譜前為何稍作停留？他翻看幾頁，略看圖片和標題，再決定回家讀哪章。）

options.en: He got a quick sense of the book.
options.zh: 他快速了解書本大概。

options.en: He browsed some pages before choosing.
options.zh: 他選擇前略看了幾頁。

options.en: He leafed through the book.
options.zh: 他隨手翻閱了那本書。

options.en: He checked its layout without reading it all.
options.zh: 他看看編排，沒有讀完整本書。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都是粗略翻看，金句用 leaf through。

scene.promptZh: 學生選參考書前先略看目錄和幾張內頁，未開始細讀。哪句最貼切？

options.en: She leafed through the book.
options.zh: 她隨手翻閱那本書。

options.en: She mastered every chapter.
options.zh: 她掌握了每一章。

options.en: She collected fallen tree leaves.
options.zh: 她收集落葉。

scene.explanationZh: 略看目錄和內頁是初步翻閱。

options.en: A reader turns a few pages of a travel guide.
options.zh: 讀者翻看旅遊指南的幾頁。

options.en: A student studies each paragraph of one chapter and checks every citation.
options.zh: 學生細讀一章每段並核對每條引文。

options.en: A shopper glances over pictures in a cookbook.
options.zh: 購物者略看食譜圖片。

contrast.explanationZh: 逐段精讀和核對引文超出隨手翻閱。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我 leafed through the report，所以已核實全部數據。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: Leafing through gives an overview; checking every figure requires closer reading.
options.zh: 隨手翻閱只得大概；核對每個數字仍須細讀。

options.en: Turning pages automatically verifies all data.
options.zh: 翻頁會自動核實所有數據。

options.en: The phrase means burning the pages.
options.zh: 片語指焚燒書頁。

dialogue.explanationZh: 初步瀏覽與完整核對不同。

speaking.en: I leafed through the exhibition catalogue and marked two photographs to study more carefully later.
speaking.zh: 我隨手翻閱展覽目錄，標記兩張照片，稍後再仔細研究。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出說話者之後會做甚麼。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：志玲在書店選一本香港步道指南，先翻看地圖、目錄和幾頁圖片；她還未核對路線的最新開放情況。用一至兩句英文描述翻閱及其限制。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出略看地圖、目錄、圖片，尚未核對路線是否開放。

examples.en: Chi-ling leafed through the walking guide, glancing at maps, contents and pictures, but she still needs to check whether its routes are open.
examples.zh: 志玲隨手翻閱步道指南，略看地圖、目錄和圖片，但仍須核對路線是否開放。

examples.en: Before buying the guide, she leafed through it for a quick overview; that did not confirm the current status of any route.
examples.zh: 買指南前，她隨手翻閱以了解大概；這並沒有確認任何路線目前的開放情況。

takeaways.en: Leaf through means browse pages for an overview.
takeaways.zh: 隨手翻閱，指翻看書頁了解大概。

takeaways.en: Leafing through a guide does not verify every detail.
takeaways.zh: 隨手翻閱指南不等於核實每個細節。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Source is guide-written provenance; practice scenes are newly written. No human or release approval is implied.

brief.meaningEn: A chaotic situation in which effective rules or moderation are absent; a situation can descend into one.
brief.meaningZh: 缺乏有效規則或管理的無序混亂局面；情況亦可逐步陷入此局面。
brief.grammar: A free-for-all is a hyphenated noun. Be/become a free-for-all describes a state; descend into a free-for-all describes deterioration; a bit of a free-for-all softens the degree.
brief.register: Forum moderation meeting: an organiser warns about an unmoderated public discussion.
brief.boundaryZh: 熱烈討論不必然是無序混亂；a bit of a 可指程度較輕，仍須看到規則失效。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是活動免費，也不是大家可自由發言就必定混亂。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分辨熱烈但有序、輕度混亂，以及秩序逐步崩潰。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 140, row 2; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Without moderation, the forum risks descending into a free-for-all.

listening.en: At the community fair, booth signs were missing and visitors wandered into several queues at once. The entrance became a free-for-all until volunteers added directions.
listening.zh: 社區嘉年華的攤位標示不見了，訪客同時排進幾條隊。入口一度變成無序混亂的局面，直到義工加上指示。
listening.promptZh: a free-for-all 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: An entrance without effective queuing order.
options.zh: 入口沒有有效排隊秩序。

options.en: An event with no admission fee.
options.zh: 一項不用付入場費的活動。

options.en: A lively but clearly directed entrance.
options.zh: 熱鬧但指示清楚的入口。

options.en: A unanimous decision by visitors.
options.zh: 訪客一致作出的決定。

listening.explanationZh: 標示缺失令幾條隊伍混在一起，指無序的局面；與免費無關。

reply.promptEn: What happened to the online debate after moderators left? Posts repeated unchecked, members shouted over one another, and no one could follow the original question.
reply.promptZh: （版主離開後網上辯論怎樣了？帖子無人審核而不斷重複，成員互相叫嚷，沒人能跟上原本問題。）

options.en: It lost the rules that kept discussion usable.
options.zh: 討論失去維持秩序的規則。

options.en: It became increasingly hard to follow.
options.zh: 內容愈來愈難跟上。

options.en: It descended into a free-for-all.
options.zh: 它陷入無序混亂。

options.en: Moderation failure allowed disorder to grow.
options.zh: 管理失效令混亂擴大。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均根據管理失效和秩序惡化作答。

scene.promptZh: 小型家長日有幾個攤位標示不清，家長稍微互相插隊，但義工很快重新排好；哪句最貼切？

options.en: For a short while, it was a bit of a free-for-all.
options.zh: 有一小段時間，場面有點無序混亂。

options.en: Everyone followed a clear queue from the start.
options.zh: 所有人一開始就依清楚次序排隊。

options.en: The event was free of admission charges.
options.zh: 活動免收入場費。

scene.explanationZh: 短暫插隊顯示輕度混亂；a bit of a 緩和程度，並非免費。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不足以使用此片語？

options.en: A chair uses timed turns, and a heated debate still follows them.
options.zh: 主席設定限時輪流發言，激烈辯論仍遵守次序。

options.en: A discussion loses its moderator and becomes a shouting match.
options.zh: 討論失去主持後變成互相叫嚷。

options.en: A queue collapses when no one checks turns.
options.zh: 無人維持次序，隊伍陷入混亂。

contrast.explanationZh: 意見激烈但規則仍有效，未陷入無序。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「有人反對我，所以會議是 free-for-all。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: Disagreement alone does not mean a meeting has descended into a free-for-all; we need evidence that its rules broke down.
options.zh: 單有異議不表示會議已陷入無序混亂；須看規則是否失效。

options.en: Any opposing view means rules have failed.
options.zh: 任何反對意見都代表規則失效。

options.en: The phrase means everyone receives free tickets.
options.zh: 片語指人人獲免費門票。

dialogue.explanationZh: 判斷重點是秩序，不是意見一致與否。

speaking.en: The public forum descended into a free-for-all after speakers ignored the time limit and shouted across the room.
speaking.zh: 發言者無視時間限制、隔着會場互相叫嚷後，公眾論壇陷入無序混亂。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪項規則被忽視。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：屋苑會議原本每人兩分鐘發言；主持中途離開後，數人同時搶咪高風、發言時間無人控制，議題無法繼續。用一至兩句英文描述秩序變化，勿把異議本身當成混亂。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出原有兩分鐘規則、主持離開後搶咪與無人控時、秩序惡化。

examples.en: After the chair left, the residents’ meeting descended into a free-for-all: several people grabbed the microphone at once and the two-minute rule stopped working.
examples.zh: 主持離開後，居民會議陷入無序混亂：幾人同時搶咪高風，兩分鐘發言規則也失效。

examples.en: The meeting began to descend into a free-for-all when the chair left, speakers talked over one another, and no one enforced the time limit.
examples.zh: 主持離開、發言者互相蓋過對方聲音，又無人執行時間限制時，會議開始陷入無序混亂。

takeaways.en: A free-for-all is a disorderly situation without effective rules.
takeaways.zh: a free-for-all 指缺乏有效規則的無序局面。

takeaways.en: A situation may descend into a free-for-all, or be a bit of a free-for-all.
takeaways.zh: 情況可逐步陷入無序混亂，也可只是有點混亂。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Source is guide-written provenance; practice scenes are newly written. No human or release approval is implied.

brief.meaningEn: Go beyond an accepted ethical or social boundary in conduct.
brief.meaningZh: 行為超出社會或情境中可接受的界線。
brief.grammar: Cross/crosses/crossed the line or a line; both mark an unacceptable boundary. The points of reference may be a shared threshold (the) or one boundary among others (a). Specify the conduct, not a literal painted line.
brief.register: Digital-citizenship discussion: a teacher explains why recording strangers without permission is unacceptable.
brief.boundaryZh: 要說明哪項行為、哪條界線，不是單靠自己不喜歡便判定越界。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是跨過地上的實際線，也不等於所有批評都不可接受。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出具體越界行為和涉及的同意或私隱原則。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 140, row 6; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Filming strangers without consent crosses the line.

listening.en: A customer challenged a refund decision, then sent threats to the clerk’s personal account. The threats crossed the line.
listening.zh: 顧客質疑退款決定後，向職員的私人帳戶發出恐嚇訊息。恐嚇行為越過了可接受界線。
listening.promptZh: crossed the line 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: Threatening the clerk went beyond acceptable conduct.
options.zh: 恐嚇職員超出可接受行為。

options.en: The customer stepped over a painted line.
options.zh: 顧客跨過畫在地上的線。

options.en: Respectful disagreement itself was forbidden.
options.zh: 有禮的異議本身被禁止。

options.en: The clerk gave permission to receive threats.
options.zh: 職員准許對方恐嚇自己。

listening.explanationZh: 越界點是向私人帳戶發恐嚇訊息，並非單純質疑退款。

reply.promptEn: A club member disagrees with a proposal, then shares another member’s private medical message in the group chat to embarrass them. What changed?
reply.promptZh: （社團成員不同意提案，之後把另一成員的私人醫療訊息貼到群組，令對方難堪。哪項行為改變了事情性質？）

options.en: Sharing private information went beyond fair disagreement.
options.zh: 公開私人資料超出合理異議。

options.en: The medical message should not have been exposed.
options.zh: 醫療訊息不應被公開。

options.en: Posting that private message crossed the line.
options.zh: 張貼那則私人訊息越過可接受界線。

options.en: The member violated a clear privacy boundary.
options.zh: 該成員觸犯明確私隱界線。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均把越界點放在公開私人醫療訊息，而非單純反對。

scene.promptZh: 有人在比賽後批評判決，之後公開裁判住址並鼓勵陌生人上門。哪句最貼切？

options.en: Publishing the address crossed the line.
options.zh: 公開住址越過可接受界線。

options.en: Any disagreement with a referee is forbidden.
options.zh: 任何對裁判的異議都被禁止。

options.en: The person crossed a painted sports line.
options.zh: 此人跨過球場畫線。

scene.explanationZh: 公開私人住址是具體越界行為。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不足以說 cross the line？

options.en: A student respectfully questions a teacher’s reasoning during discussion.
options.zh: 學生討論時有禮地質疑老師的理據。

options.en: A user posts a neighbour’s private phone number without permission.
options.zh: 用戶未經准許公開鄰居私人電話。

options.en: A player threatens an official after a match.
options.zh: 球員賽後恐嚇裁判。

contrast.explanationZh: 有禮的討論不等於越過行為界線。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我不喜歡你的意見，所以你 crossed the line。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: Disagreement alone need not cross a line; identify the actual conduct and boundary.
options.zh: 單純異議不一定越過可接受界線；須指出具體行為與界線。

options.en: Anything I dislike is automatically misconduct.
options.zh: 凡我不喜歡的事都自動屬不當行為。

options.en: The phrase refers to crossing a road only.
options.zh: 片語只指過馬路。

dialogue.explanationZh: 要有可說明的行為界線。

speaking.en: The moderator crossed a line by mocking a speaker’s disability; disagreeing with the proposal itself would have been fair.
speaking.zh: 主持嘲笑發言者的殘疾，越過了可接受界線；單純不同意提案本來可以合理。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪個行為越界、哪個行為本可接受。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學生會候選人公開辯論午膳政策，這本來合理；其中一人把對手與輔導員的私人談話截圖發到全校群組。用一至兩句英文說明哪項行為越界及原因。
writing.selfCheckZh: 區分公開政策辯論與未經同意公開私人輔導談話，點出私隱界線。

examples.en: Debating lunch policy was fair, but posting a private counselling chat to the whole school crossed the line because it exposed confidential information.
examples.zh: 辯論午膳政策是合理的，但向全校發出私人輔導談話越過可接受界線，因為這公開了機密資料。

examples.en: The candidate crossed the line by sharing a screenshot of the rival’s private counselling conversation; the disagreement over lunch policy did not justify that privacy breach.
examples.zh: 候選人分享對手私人輔導對話截圖，越過可接受界線；午膳政策上的異議不能成為侵犯私隱的理由。

takeaways.en: Cross the line means go beyond acceptable conduct.
takeaways.zh: 越過界線，指行為超出可接受範圍。

takeaways.en: A remark can cross a line when it violates a clear boundary; disagreement alone need not.
takeaways.zh: 言論若觸犯清楚界線便可能越界；單純異議不一定越界。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Source is guide-written provenance; practice scenes are newly written. No human or release approval is implied.

brief.meaningEn: Overwork a person until they are exhausted.
brief.meaningZh: 使人因過度工作而筋疲力盡。
brief.grammar: Run someone into the ground; the object can be a person or group. Passive: be run into the ground. Ran is the past form.
brief.register: Workplace discussion: a union representative warns managers that repeated overtime can exhaust staff.
brief.boundaryZh: 辛苦的一天未必等於長期過勞；要看工作量和休息是否持續失衡。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是把人實際壓入泥土，也不是稱讚其勤奮。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述造成疲勞的工作安排，不把過勞美化為敬業。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 141, row 13; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: No employee should be run into the ground by overtime.

listening.en: The manager scheduled double shifts for weeks with no recovery days. By the final weekend, the kitchen team had been run into the ground.
listening.zh: 經理連續幾週安排雙更，沒有恢復休息日。到了最後一個週末，廚房團隊已被操勞得筋疲力盡。
listening.promptZh: run into the ground 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: Overworked until exhausted.
options.zh: 因過度工作而筋疲力盡。

options.en: Buried physically in soil.
options.zh: 實際被埋進泥土。

options.en: Given plenty of rest.
options.zh: 得到充足休息。

options.en: Praised for one busy but balanced day.
options.zh: 因忙碌但平衡的一天受讚。

listening.explanationZh: 連續雙更且沒有休息，使團隊過勞。

reply.promptEn: Why did the theatre crew ask for a new rota? They had worked late rehearsals every night for three weeks, with early calls each morning and no full day off.
reply.promptZh: （劇團工作人員為何要求新更表？他們連續三週每晚排練至深夜，翌日清早又要上班，沒有一整天休息。）

options.en: The schedule left too little recovery time.
options.zh: 更表留下的恢復時間太少。

options.en: They were exhausted by sustained overwork.
options.zh: 持續過勞令他們筋疲力盡。

options.en: The rota was running them into the ground.
options.zh: 更表把他們操勞得筋疲力盡。

options.en: Repeated late and early shifts were wearing them out.
options.zh: 反覆晚班和早班令他們疲憊。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都依據連續過勞與欠缺休息作答。

scene.promptZh: 清潔團隊連續一個月每週工作七天，主管仍加班次，員工多次疲倦病倒。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The rota is running the cleaners into the ground.
options.zh: 更表正把清潔員操勞得筋疲力盡。

options.en: The team has a well-rested schedule.
options.zh: 團隊有充分休息的更表。

options.en: The cleaners are working underground.
options.zh: 清潔員在地底工作。

scene.explanationZh: 長期無休加班與病倒支持過勞。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不足以支持此片語？

options.en: A busy festival shift is followed by agreed time off and adequate rest.
options.zh: 忙碌節慶班次後有預先安排的假期及充足休息。

options.en: A manager adds weeks of double shifts without recovery days.
options.zh: 經理連續幾週安排雙更且無恢復休息日。

options.en: A team works nightly overtime for months and falls ill from fatigue.
options.zh: 團隊連續數月每晚加班，因疲倦病倒。

contrast.explanationZh: 忙碌但有足夠休息，未見持續過勞。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「他們被 run into the ground，證明主管很會激勵人。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: Running workers into the ground is harmful overwork, not effective motivation.
options.zh: 把員工操勞到筋疲力盡是有害的過勞，不是有效激勵。

options.en: Exhaustion proves excellent management.
options.zh: 筋疲力盡證明管理出色。

options.en: It means workers were put under the floor.
options.zh: 它指工人被放到地板下。

speaking.en: The volunteers were run into the ground by six weeks of late-night sorting with no rest days.
speaking.zh: 義工連續六週深夜整理物資，沒有休息日，被操勞得筋疲力盡。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出令義工過勞的安排。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：慈善熱線原本每人每週四更，遇上活動後連續五週每週七更，沒有補假，幾名接線員因疲勞請病假。用一至兩句英文說明安排造成甚麼問題，勿稱這是值得讚揚的效率。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出四更變七更、持續五週無補假、接線員疲勞請病假。

examples.en: When four shifts rose to seven a week for five weeks without time off, the helpline operators were run into the ground; several took sick leave from exhaustion.
examples.zh: 接線員原本每週四更，連續五週增至七更又沒有補假，結果被操勞得筋疲力盡；幾人因疲勞請病假。

examples.en: The charity changed from four to seven shifts a week for five weeks and offered no recovery days. That schedule was running operators into the ground; several took sick leave from exhaustion.
examples.zh: 慈善機構連續五週把每週四更改為七更，又沒有恢復休息日。這更表正把接線員操勞得筋疲力盡；幾人因疲勞請病假。

takeaways.en: Run someone into the ground means overwork them to exhaustion.
takeaways.zh: 把人操勞到筋疲力盡，指過度工作令其疲憊。

takeaways.en: Do not praise a schedule that runs workers into the ground.
takeaways.zh: 不應稱讚把員工操勞得筋疲力盡的更表。
